body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — (name sources, carried stable id) every Dioxus element node carries its stable id as AccessKit `author_id`, no TextRun / document-root / Window node does (contract/accessibility-tree/author-id), and the shell builds and refreshes the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree` so a wrapper's override reaches it. A virtual tree node is a fourth kind of node the author-id loop must recognise (F7 A: the loop checks the virtual map first), and it must enter through that same override.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot became a consumer of the accessibility tree, taking role, name and focus from it with no second role or name mapping. This is the basis of decision/snapshot-reads-accessibility-tree and decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree, and so of reading a virtual node from the tree rather than from its declaration.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — the actionable-key rule: every actionable element (focusable, interactive role or listener) reads an author key, checked by `unkeyed_actionable`, which takes the role from the tree. Trap: never satisfy it by adding a tabindex or a role. A virtual node with an interactive role in the tree must not trip the check or be held as unkeyed, and its `{owner}///{key}` id is not an element key.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — the snapshot reads `enabled` (the presence of `disabled`), `checked` and `value` from the element because the tree gives an element none of them. A virtual node has no element, so F8 A's declared `disabled`, written on the virtual tree node and read as `enabled`, is a new source for this reading that has to be stated beside the element rule (contract/snapshot/enabled).

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — `Snapshot::to_text` is a reader of the snapshot model alone, one line per snapshot node, role and name the node's. Virtual nodes put in the model reach the text form, and through it every carrier that F3 A widens, by this rule.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — the tree is refreshed on change from the engine's changed set, and `Snapshot::diff` became a reader of the snapshot model: a text change is reported on the element whose name it changes, never as a text-run entry. This is the origin of decision/changed-set-marks and contract/snapshot-diff/entries, which the virtual-node diff (added, removed or changed by id) extends. F11 A keeps declarations unmarked.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the founder ratified the refresh on change and the changed-set contract (decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change, decision/changed-set-marks). F11 A is the founder's word not to amend these ratified rows for declaration changes; the row stays as ratified.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a fresh harness document holds a non-empty set, so a check reading the set as one step's change drains it first (decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set). This bears on any check that a declaration change marks nothing, and on the virtual click's settle-then-diff.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the driver's `disabled` cause is worded on the snapshot's presence reading. Rule: the entry that detects `disabled` reads the snapshot's `enabled`, never an attribute value. The virtual node's `disabled` refusal must come from its snapshot `enabled`, fed by the declared bool, and not from a separate check.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — `disabled` is detected in `Session::run` on `enabled == Some(false)`, the first screen-level check, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was (contract/driver-refusal/disabled, contract/driver-actions/disabled). This fixes the order and no-dispatch rule that the virtual node's refusals (stale / not-found, then disabled, off-screen, covered) must keep.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — (the tree states selected, toggled and invalid) the builder writes the states on the node and the snapshot takes them from the tree, never from the element; one parser per attribute keeps the snapshot and the tree in agreement. This is the precedent for writing the virtual node's state (declared disabled) on its tree node and reading it from there.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result reads the snapshot model and nothing else, and a `snapshot` block equals `Session::run`'s screen text (contract/mcp-result/snapshot). Under F3 A virtual nodes reach MCP only through this path, with no new carrier.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — the node keys' help and `DiffNode::differs` are readers of the model, closed words only. `differs` names readings in node-key order (contract/snapshot-diff/differs), and that order applies to a changed virtual node. No node key is added.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — the driver's `screenshot` reads the model's bounds: an element shot by stable id is its bounds rounded outward and cropped, and a shot changes nothing (contract/driver-screenshot/element-shot). F10 B makes `screenshot --id` on a virtual id read `not-found`, a stated limit against this contract.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — (`disabled` by presence) disabled-ness is keyed one way, by the attribute's presence (founder's word). The sibling entry has Enter and Space dispatch a synthetic Click (decision/synthetic-click-at-node-centre). These are the origins of decision/disabled-by-attribute-presence, decision/disabled-by-presence and decision/enabled-by-disabled-presence, which the declared `disabled` bool on a virtual node sits beside without an attribute.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — `aria-disabled` writes a tree node's disabled, but the snapshot's `enabled` never reads it (decision/enabled-by-disabled-presence: aria-disabled moves no snapshot reading). Trap: F8 A writes the declared `disabled` on the virtual tree node and has the snapshot read it as `enabled`. That is a tree-sourced enabled reading which this row currently excludes for elements, so the row's clause must be qualified without letting `aria-disabled` in.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled`) a truthy `inert` takes focusability, hits and the tree from its subtree, a hit passes through an inert element, and `disabled` is narrowed to form controls (decision/inert-subtree-excluded, decision/inert-element-takes-no-hit, contract/hit-testing/inert; ratified 2026-10-18). A canvas under `inert` or hidden must take its virtual children out of the tree, and a click on one must not land.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — `Snapshot::text_parts` reads the model through the text form, every node id on exactly one line (contract/snapshot-text/parts). Virtual node lines and ids are bound by this.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the tree's focus falls back to the window) `build_accessibility_tree` writes focus only where the focused node is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX` (contract/accessibility-tree/focus, contract/accessibility-tree/root). F7 A's focus writer has to check the virtual map first, and the tree must never name a node it did not build.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (what the snapshot reads of an open list; covered; the changed set) the snapshot builder reads `select_list_bounds(node)` before the client rect, so a row's bounds come from something other than its DOM box. That is the nearest precedent for virtual bounds from a region moved by the canvas origin. No `expanded` node key was added. A driver click on an element under an open list is refused `covered` (contract/driver-click-refusals/covered). A single select's list open/close marks the changed set. Precedents for the virtual bounds arm, the `covered` reading and the no-new-key rule.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — `NodeState.clickable` is read from the vdom walk's current click listeners (contract/snapshot/clickable, contract/snapshot-node/clickable, contract/snapshot-text/clickable). The read-only UI graph holds one node per snapshot node (decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node, decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values). `stand_graph` asserts that no served id holds the reserved separator `///`, the `{owner}///{key}` form spelled by `virtual_node_id` (contract/node-id/reserved-separator). This chunk serves `///` ids for the first time: the separator contract and the stand_graph assertion are what change. F12 A has a virtual node read `clickable` false, and F9 A excludes virtual nodes from the graph to keep one node per snapshot node.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — `actionable_nodes` lists the UI graph's nodes, `keyed` true where the id holds no `/`. The `actions` verb answers each id-taking verb with the cause `check_target` would refuse, a node with no element reading `stale`. A virtual id holds `///` (keyed false) and resolves to no element, so the actions reader and the refusal causes (`stale`, `not-found`) need care. Exploration is held out under F9 A.
**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — `handler_coverage` is one more reader of `DioxusDocument::graph`. With virtual nodes kept out of the graph (F9 A), it must not see them through the snapshot.

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` took the select-list scroll qualifier. This is part of the row history that F11 A leaves unamended (a declaration change writes no mark).

**2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts** — `~ decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change` and `~ decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`: the tree is pushed in a redraw after style resolve only when the changed set is non-empty, through the document trait's method. `~ contract/accessibility-tree/hidden-and-inert-nodes`, `~ decision/hidden-content-excluded-from-a11y-tree` and `~ decision/hidden-content-excluded` added `visibility: collapse`. Under F11 A a declaration change alone never pushes a new platform tree, and a hidden canvas's virtual nodes fall under these exclusion rows.

**2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` (highlight moves mark), `~ decision/snapshot-reads-accessibility-tree` and `~ decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree` (highlighted taken from the tree), and the tree naming the highlighted option as active descendant. This is the latest precedent for a new tree-sourced snapshot reading and its row edits, which a virtual node's tree-written state follows.

**2026-11-21-engine-debts** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` reached its current wording (post-layout focus loss too) and `~ decision/tab-and-shift-tab-move-focus` changed. This is the row text F11 A leaves as is, and the scope's CARRY `cry-t4af3d26` names this row as left unamended.

**2026-11-21-single-select-sized-as-a-list-box** — `~ decision/single-select-engine-overlay-list` (a drop-down alone opens the overlay) and `~ contract/accessibility-tree/select-expanded`. These are the current texts of the picked select rows behind the `covered` refusal and the expanded reading that a virtual node does not touch.

**2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts** — ratified the PROVISIONAL hidden-content rows (`decision/hidden-content-excluded`, `contract/accessibility-tree/hidden-and-inert-nodes`, `decision/hidden-content-excluded-from-a11y-tree`) in the founder's own word. Those rows now stand ratified, and any change to them for virtual nodes needs the founder.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — `docs/capabilities.md` publishes the accessibility reach (tier 0) and is edited by hand, since its pin reads none of the claims (decision/capability-statement-reach-by-hand, decision/accessibility-reach-tier-0). F3 A lists `docs/capabilities.md` among the surfaces now carrying virtual ids and names, and its stated limits (F10 B, F12 A) go there by hand.

**2026-11-18-capability-statement** — `~ decision/capability-statement-reach-by-hand` · why: the pin reads only the a11y leg's file count and no check reads the rest. Any reach or limit line this chunk adds is unchecked.

**2026-11-18-a11y-re-read** — `~ decision/removed-focused-node-drops-focus`: focus drops to the root element and the tree's focus names the window. A virtual click focuses the canvas, and the focus writer's virtual-map check must keep the window fallback.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** — (the enabled-state walks) the `&dyn Document` tree is shown equal to the document's, carrying stable ids only (decision/adapter-tree-is-document-tree). The platform adapter is an F3 A exit, so the adapter tree must hold the same virtual nodes and ids.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** — (the `lint` verb) a contrast finding carries the node's id, with ids, closed words and numbers only (contract/lint-contrast-finding/id). F9 A holds virtual nodes out of the lint, so no finding carries a `///` id.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the lint's closed-select overlap ended) `overlaps` skips a closed select's options by reading the element, not the role. This is a precedent for the lint excluding snapshot nodes by kind, as F9 A's exclusion in `lint.rs` must.

**2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** — `+ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only`: Circle Drawer's drawing area is one named canvas node, and its circles reach no snapshot or tree. Making Circle Drawer's circles virtual nodes is outside this chunk, so its circles keep reading as this row states.

**2026-11-24T06-11-11-wrap** — `~ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` state provisional → standing, ratified by the founder. The canvas-node row this chunk's fixture canvas sits beside now stands.

**2026-11-24-canvas-draw-commands** — `~ decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model` and `~ decision/snapshot-model-single-source`: the canvas read is no reader of the snapshot model. This is the first split of these rows between snapshot readers and canvas reads, which this chunk changes by moving virtual nodes into the snapshot model.

**2026-11-24-canvas-lint** — `~ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only`: canvas labels reach the lint as truncated boxes with no text, PROVISIONAL on the delegate's confirm. This is the nearest canvas-to-lint path, and it must stay separate from the F9 A lint exclusion of virtual nodes.

**2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-declared** — `~ decision/snapshot-model-single-source` and `~ decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`: the virtual-node read of one canvas's declared nodes is no reader of the snapshot model and feeds no carrier. This chunk inverts that, putting virtual nodes in the tree, the snapshot and every carrier (F3 A), so both rows' virtual-node clauses must be re-said. This is the CARRY `cry-qprhfz5u` inversion.

**2026-11-24-upstream-sync-ahead-of-inside-the-canvas** — `+ absence/keyboard-drag-and-drop`: no keyboard or assistive-technology route exists for drag and drop. It is a picked absence of the scope area. Keyboard reach to virtual nodes likewise stays out of scope («Canvas keyboard path»).

A canvas's declared virtual nodes (key, AccessKit role, name, content-box region, id `{owner}///{key}`) enter the accessibility tree as children of their canvas's tree node, each with an even-versioned tree id that no DOM id collides with.
The snapshot reads each virtual node from the tree as a node (id, role, name, state, bounds), and the snapshot diff names a virtual node added, removed or changed by its id.
The driver's `click` takes a virtual node's id, acts at its region's centre and returns once settled with the diff; its refusals (stale or not-found, then disabled, off-screen, covered) hold for a virtual node in the run path's one order.
A virtual node declaration gains a declared disabled flag, written on the tree node and read by the snapshot as its enabled; the UI graph, the visual lint and exploration hold virtual nodes out.
The owed mutation control of the declared-nodes check is re-read: its snapshot half inverts into this chunk's check, entering with its red reading, and its graph half stands.

body: The accessibility tree gains virtual tree nodes as children of their canvas's node, each carrying its declared role and name; the tree still never names a node it did not build, and its root and focus rules hold.

A virtual tree node's AccessKit id is even-versioned (canvas slot index low, 2·(n+1) high) so it collides with no DOM node id; the three readers that decode a tree id — the snapshot builder, the author-id loop, the focus writer — check the virtual map before decoding a DOM id.

The snapshot takes a virtual node's role, name and state from the tree, never from a second mapping; its id is `{owner}///{key}`, the reserved separator `///` with the key inside it, and its bounds are its region moved to the page by its canvas's content-box origin and transforms.

A virtual node's enabled reading comes from its declared disabled flag written on the tree node, so the driver's disabled refusal fires on a declared-disabled virtual node; the snapshot's enabled for elements still follows the disabled attribute's presence.

A virtual node's clickable reads false in the snapshot node and its text form, a stated limit; its other state readings are closed values inside the existing node fields — no new snapshot node field or state token.
The snapshot diff names a virtual node added, removed or changed by its id, through the existing diff entries and differs fields.
The driver's click resolves a virtual id and lands a primary pointer click at its region's centre on the canvas, the widget reading the point; it returns once settled with the diff, as on an element.

The driver's refusal causes hold for a virtual node in the one run-path order — stale or not-found, then disabled, off-screen, covered — with nothing run; off-screen reads the region's centre against the canvas's visible region, and covered reads DOM coverage of the region's centre only (another virtual node over it inside the canvas unseen), a stated limit.
Only click resolves a virtual id: type, scroll, screenshot by id, layout by id and canvas by id read a virtual id not-found, a stated limit.

A virtual node's name and id ride today's accessible-name and stable-id exits — the platform adapter, the snapshot text and diff on the session socket, the command line, MCP results, the session recording and kept-check replay, the cold-agent pipe — with no new carrier, refusal cause, exit, session error, log field or span; a boundary widening answered by the founder (F3 A).

A declaration change raises no invalidation signal and writes no changed-set mark (F11 A); the changed-set marks and the tree refresh on change stay as ratified, every driver reading being current because the snapshot rebuilds the tree per read.
The UI graph, the visual lint and exploration exclude a virtual node until a later chunk (F9 A), so the graph stays one node per element snapshot node and the lint reads no finding on a virtual node.
The snapshot model stays the single source its readers share; the canvas read and the virtual-node read remain no readers of it, and the readers stay behind the accessibility feature.

The owed mutation control of the declared-nodes check «a declaring canvas puts nothing on the snapshot or graph» is proved: the snapshot half inverts into an assertion that the virtual node is on the snapshot, the graph half stands, and the control enters the plan with its red reading.
The proof surface is a fixture canvas a test declares; checks assert over the built accessibility tree and the snapshot, and no plan step deletes a worktree or build directory.
A row resting only on a delegate's answer (F7 A, F9 A, F10 B, F12 A) lands provisional; the founder's own answers (F3 A, F11 A, F2 A with F8 A) are ratified ground.

each new accessibility test file runs in the a11y CI leg and the accessibility checks gate CI

Text contrast thresholds, the stand's contrast tables, stand accent colour and the select list's colours and motion: the chunk paints nothing new.

ARIA attribute reads and hidden-content rules (aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-expanded, hidden, display none, inert): a virtual node carries no attributes and is read from its declaration.
Select and list box semantics — options, optgroups, open-list rows, expanded, highlighted row, select value: untouched.

**2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-declared** (Standard Contracts: 5 rows) — landed `contract/nodes-widgets/virtual-nodes`, `contract/dioxus-bridge/virtual-nodes`, `contract/dioxus-bridge/virtual-node-refusal` and re-said `contract/stable-element-id/virtual-node-id` and `contract/dioxus-bridge/virtual-node-id`: `{owner}///{key}` is given in process only to a canvas's taken nodes, "no carrier serves it". This chunk's whole build sits on that read. Putting virtual nodes in the snapshot and its carriers makes "no carrier serves it" false, so both id rows need re-wording. `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `disabled` (F8 A), which amends the declaration contract. The three added rows are PROVISIONAL on a delegate's word.

**2026-11-25-virtual-nodes-declared** (Established Decisions: 2 rows) — added `decision/virtual-node-role-is-accesskit-role` and `decision/virtual-node-declaration-marks-nothing`, both PROVISIONAL. The second hands the changed-set mark and the invalidation signal to "the first reader that refreshes", which is this entry. F11 A (the founder's word) keeps the absence: no mark and no signal, with readings current because the snapshot rebuilds the tree on each read. So the row's "yet / first refreshing reader" wording and its provisional state must be settled here.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the reserved virtual-node id form) — reserved the fifth id form `{owner}///{key}` beside the four tiers, spelled by `VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR` and `virtual_node_id`, and it rested on a measured "no served id holds `///`". `stand_graph` asserts that no served id holds `///`. Under F9 A the graph keeps that true, but a snapshot assertion of the same kind now inverts.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the UI graph reader; the graph crosses the ratified carriers) — `DioxusDocument::graph` gives one `GraphNode` per snapshot node in pre-order. This is why a virtual node put in the snapshot reaches the graph unless it is excluded (F9 A, `graph.rs`). The graph's crossing list (ids, names, closed flags) is the precedent this chunk's widening follows.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the snapshot's `clickable` reading) — added `NodeState.clickable`, read from the vdom walk's current listeners and an `is_disabled` form control. A virtual node has no listeners, so under F12 A its `clickable` reads false, a stated limit. The Reading/NODE_FIELDS growth here is the precedent for the closed-bool shape of any new reading.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — set snapshot membership: a node is an accessibility-tree node with an `author_id` whose element resolves through `get_node`, and each field comes from an existing reader. The standing rule is that the snapshot derives no role or name of its own. This is the reason a virtual tree node reads nothing until the builder gets its own arm (scope premise `snapshot.rs:164-179`), and the arm must take role and name from the tree, not re-derive them.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — `DioxusDocument`'s `accessibility_tree` override sets each element's AccessKit `author_id` to its stable id, so the id reaches both the harness tree and the shell's platform tree. That override is where virtual children of a canvas node and their ids get added. The trap it recorded: a feature-gated item can compile out under `-p blitz-tests`.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — the four-tier grammar and its distinctness, where only an anchored path holds `//`. `contract/stable-element-id/tier-distinctness` must still hold once `{owner}///{key}` ids are served. Its trap: `UnkeyedActionable.node` is a process-local `NodeId`, so no wire form may carry it.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — added the changed set and its refresh-then-drain rule (ratified 2026-10-07), with the diff explicitly not derived from it. This is the basis for F11 A: a virtual node's add/remove/change shows in the diff because the diff compares two snapshots, while the changed set stays unmarked (`decision/diff-not-engine-changed-set`, `decision/changed-set-refresh-then-drain`).

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** (Cross-cutting Patterns) — `~ decision/changed-set-write-sites` gained its select-list exception. This is one of the ratified rows a declaration mark would amend for every document (CARRY `cry-t4af3d26`), which F11 A declines.

**2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts** (Cross-cutting Patterns: 2 rows) — `~ decision/changed-set-write-sites` gained "moving its highlight to a new row" as a write site, ratified. It is the latest precedent of a non-element reading (a list row) being added to the closed write-site list, which is the step this chunk deliberately does not take for virtual nodes. Its Standard Contracts entries added the `highlighted` node key and the tree's active descendant, a closed-bool precedent inside the ratified carriers.

**2026-11-21-engine-debts** (Cross-cutting Patterns: 2 rows) — `~ decision/changed-set-write-sites` except gained "a focus given up after a layout marks its node". This is the row's current text, the one any amendment here must quote. The chunk also added the post-layout focus fixup to `contract/event-dispatch/focus-change` (no events) and extended `decision/hit-focus-form-engine-changes`.

**2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts** (Standard Contracts: 3 rows; Cross-cutting Patterns: 4 rows) — moved the platform-tree refresh to the redraw after resolve, gated on a non-empty changed set (`decision/accessibility-tree-refresh-on-change`, `contract/accessibility-tree/platform-refresh`, `decision/a11y-rebuild-on-nonempty-changed-set`). With F11 A's no-mark, a declaration change alone does not refresh the platform adapter's tree. That is a consequence to state now that virtual nodes ride the adapter exit. **2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the tree's focus falls back to the window) — `build_accessibility_tree` writes `focus` only where `focus_node_id` is among the built nodes, else the window (`contract/accessibility-tree/focus`). This is one of the three tree-id decoders F7 A says must check the virtual map first. An even-versioned virtual tree id must never be decoded as a DOM `NodeId` here.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — built the refusal order for click/type: `stale` when the session's record holds the id, else `not-found`, then `disabled` · `off-screen` · `covered`. It also added `SeenIds` (`decision/seen-ids-record-bounded`), the click point at the centre of the snapshot's `bounds`, and the rules "a refused call runs nothing" and "visibility read from geometry, never from a hit". This chunk runs a virtual id through exactly this order, and the record must hold virtual ids for `stale` to fire.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` is the one entry point that runs a call. It validates first and resolves ids through `element_ids()` and `get_node`, and nothing resolved outlives a call (`decision/validated-commands-only`). The virtual arm for `click` (F10 B) must live inside this run path, not beside it.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actions read and the shared per-verb target check) — introduced the crate-private `check_target`, the one per-verb target check called by the four id-taking arms and by `Session::actions`, with `locate` ending in `target_of`. A virtual click target has to pass through it for the disabled/off-screen/covered order to hold "in the run path's one order". `actionable_nodes` reads the UI graph's nodes, so the graph exclusion (F9 A) also keeps virtual nodes out of `actions`.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — causes closed at eight (`decision/refusal-causes-closed-at-eight`), a refusal holding nothing a call supplied, one verb table with no second one. This chunk adds no cause, so a virtual node's limits must be said through the existing causes' fixed texts.

body: The element id's virtual form `{owner}///{key}`: a virtual node's stable id, carried wherever a stable id rides today.

The snapshot node a virtual node reads as: id, role, name, state and bounds, its bounds the region moved to the page by its canvas's content-box origin and transforms, its enabled state the declared disabled flag inverted.
A virtual node's clickable reads false, a stated limit.
The snapshot diff and the acting call's result name a virtual node added, removed or changed by its id.
The driver's click on a virtual id acts at its region's centre as a pointer event, the widget hearing it in its content-box frame, and returns once settled with the diff, as on an element.

The refusal causes for a virtual id — stale for an id an earlier screen read now gone, or not-found, then disabled, off-screen and covered — in the run path's one refusal order, changing nothing and echoing no input.

Off-screen reads the region's centre against the canvas's visible region; covered reads DOM coverage of the region's centre only, walking to the canvas element — a stated limit (another virtual node over it is not seen).
Only click resolves a virtual id: type, scroll, screenshot by id, layout by id and canvas by id read it not-found, a stated limit in the capability statement.
The UI graph, the lint and exploration's digest hold virtual nodes out until a later entry; the graph half of the earlier assertion that a declaring canvas puts nothing on the graph stands.
The earlier check that a declaring canvas puts nothing on the snapshot inverts for the snapshot into this entry's check; its mutation control is owed and enters the plan with its red reading.

A virtual tree node's id is even-versioned (canvas slot index low, 2·(n+1) high) so it collides with no DOM id; each reader that decodes a tree id (the snapshot builder, the author-id loop, the focus writer) checks the virtual map first, so none aliases a live DOM node.
A declaration change raises no invalidation signal and writes no changed-set mark; every driver reading is current because the snapshot rebuilds the tree per read.

A virtual node's name and id ride today's exits only — the snapshot text and diff on the session socket's call answer, the command line, the MCP server, the session recording and kept-check replay, the cold-agent pipe — with no new carrier, refusal cause, exit code, session error, log field or span.
Stand logs, the driver's log line, the session host's stderr and the MCP role's stderr carry no virtual node id or name: the first author-written canvas-side text on a carrier stays off every log.
The snapshot text of a screen holding virtual nodes stays inside the snapshot byte budget.
The proof surface is a fixture canvas a test declares (keyed, named, role-bearing regions, one declared disabled), stated in code.
The capability statement, pinned to the driver schema, names the virtual-node limits and its claim names and counts stay held to the schema.
